name: Apartheid
summary: Apartheid was the ideology and legal system of the South African National Party government from 1948 to the early 1990s. It classified people into racial groups, kept white minority dominance (baasskap), and under Verwoerd recast segregation as 'separate development', in which Black Africans were assigned to ethnic homelands. It rested on Afrikaner nationalism and Calvinist Christian-national thought, and met opposition with sweeping security and anti-communist laws.
scope: The National Party's apartheid programme from 1948 to the 1970s, centred on Hendrik Verwoerd's 'grand apartheid' and 'separate development' (Population Registration, Group Areas, Bantu Education, homelands). It excludes later reform-era changes such as the tricameral parliament, and the anti-apartheid movement. Most economic and social answers are low-confidence inferences because the doctrine was about race and nation rather than a full programme.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: not part of the doctrine.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Labour was explicitly divided by race.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred: a communist aim that the state suppressed.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred: it stressed preserving the existing order.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred: not part of the doctrine.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: unconditional state income is foreign to the doctrine.

bound-labor.rationale: Pass laws restricted African movement but no lord-bound labour system was the aim.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist thesis, which the state suppressed.

central-planning.rationale: The state heavily directed labour and residence but not an economy by plan; split.

civilizational-union.rationale: Verwoerd's vision was a southern African commonwealth, not a civilizational union; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism sought volk unity across classes; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Communism was outlawed; the doctrine saw race and nation, not class, as basic.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred: it defended its own colonial-origin white state.

conscription.rationale: Inferred: a white state controlling its own army was a stated aim.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: segregated industrial relations excluded African unions.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Apartheid sought to entrench racial hierarchy (baasskap), not to remedy it.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: whites received state support while the doctrine did not centre on welfare-dependency arguments.

decide-locally.rationale: The Bantu Authorities were set up under chiefs answerable to Pretoria; real power stayed with the central white government.

democracy-best.rationale: Verwoerd presented one-person-one-vote democracy as leading to Black domination and chose a separate white state over it.

direct-action.rationale: Extra-parliamentary action was banned as communism or treated as a security threat.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums were used for the republic among whites, but direct rule by votes was not a principle.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred: opposed to communism and egalitarian distribution.

dominated-front.rationale: Verwoerd's South Africa sought Western ties and its own commonwealth; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; opposed to ambitious state programmes beyond its aims.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The volk and community took precedence over individuals in nationalist thought; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Verwoerd withdrew from the Commonwealth in 1961 after criticism of apartheid, rejecting outside authority.

empower-police-military.rationale: Security laws and a strong police and army were central to maintaining the system.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Apartheid assigned unequal status and resources by race.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Verwoerd argued for separate national units for each group.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the sources; a technological-nationalist state would be expected to favour it.

experts-over-public.rationale: Policy was drafted by commissions (Sauer, Tomlinson) and planners; inferred, though the white electorate was the political base.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from nationalist state-directed economic policy.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from Calvinist and traditional views.

gradual-change.rationale: Inferred: defenders sought to preserve white-minority order, though many measures were themselves sweeping restructurings.

harm-principle.rationale: The Immorality and Mixed Marriages acts restricted private conduct, not merely harm to others.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The system ranked groups with whites on top; some defenders asserted innate differences, though Verwoerd framed it as national difference.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: sovereignty claims were used against foreign criticism of apartheid.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Rhetorically, homelands were presented as the historic areas of Bantu peoples under their own authorities, but control stayed with Pretoria; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights and status were assigned by racial group.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred: it was a developmentalist state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Dutch Reformed Church treated segregation as dogma and the state as Christian.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Immorality Act policed sex across racial lines and the movement shared Calvinist moral conservatism.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: not a concern of the doctrine.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: whites kept arms for security while the state limited the arming of others; the general rule was not pursued.

limit-population.rationale: Verwoerd feared Black demographic weight, but population limits were not a defined programme.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism pursued state-backed volkskapitalisme and the state controlled where and whether Africans could work, so free-market doctrine was not central.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred: the state used coercive means for a declared peaceful separate-development goal.

media-academia-power.rationale: Afrikaner nationalists distrusted the English-language press (Verwoerd as editor clashed with it); inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Verwoerd stressed that a white state controlling its own army and police was preferable to integration.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Verwoerd secured a republic in 1961, ending the link to the Crown.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Afrikaner state was cast as a Christian civilisation, with Christian National education.

nation-first.rationale: The republican nationalist government put its own course ahead of Commonwealth and world opinion.

national-rebirth.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism had revival themes after the Boer Wars but no centered rebirth demand in sources; split.

national-self-determination.rationale: Verwoerd's separate nations were each to govern themselves, and Afrikaners sought their own republic.

natural-rulers.rationale: Baasskap held that whites were entitled to rule over other groups.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred: not part of the doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: Apartheid operated through whites-only multi-party elections, though dominated by the National Party.

open-borders.rationale: Pass laws and homeland citizenship rules restricted movement and belonging by race.

organic-representation.rationale: Homelands were governed through chiefs and ethnic authorities rather than general party politics; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred: it operated through parliamentary and party structures.

political-violence-never.rationale: The state treated violence as justified for its own security and legislated against its opponents' violence.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine centred on collective volk and order.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Preserving the volk, Afrikaans and Afrikaner Christian identity was a core aim.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: security was a central state function.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred: a socialist principle treated as communism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist analysis was banned as communism.

property-fundamental.rationale: White property was protected, yet the Group Areas Act forced evictions of other groups, so property was subordinated to racial policy; adherents' view is split by group.

public-ownership.rationale: Afrikaner nationalist governments used state-led economic institutions to uplift the volk; inferred from volkskapitalisme and the state's directing role.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Population Registration, Group Areas and Separate Amenities acts did exactly this.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Labour was channelled by race through pass laws and Bantu Education into cheap labouring work; a high-wage policy is inferred to be foreign to it.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Calvinist and Christian-national outlook placed faith above reason.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Mixed: influx control restricted Africans' movement into cities, while whites were not targets of restriction. Inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred only: the state shaped the economy for Afrikaner and racial aims rather than on a regulate-or-deregulate axis.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred: the state's response to opposition was banning and detention rather than reform.

restore-past-order.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism was a preservationist, volk-centred movement; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The state restricted dissent and enforced racial hierarchy; it did not regard racial advocacy as a harm to be restricted. Inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Policy was driven by doctrine of separate nations rather than pragmatic results.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: a state that built industry and cities on migrant labour had no place for a hunter-gatherer ideal.

revive-national-language.rationale: Afrikaans was promoted over Dutch and in white schools and became a national marker.

revolution-justified.rationale: The state outlawed communism and extra-parliamentary opposition, treating revolution as the threat it existed to suppress.

right-to-secede.rationale: Homelands were to be separate nation-units, but no general right of regions to secede was asserted.

rule-by-example.rationale: The state relied on laws and punishments.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from Dutch Reformed Calvinist moral conservatism.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education was state-run and separated by race under Bantu Education.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The volk's collective good was prioritised; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Afrikaner state was presented as Christian, with the Dutch Reformed Church backing segregation.

single-common-good.rationale: Afrikaner unity ideals existed, but multiple national groups were recognised; split.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred: collectivist ownership was associated with communism.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred: not part of the doctrine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from volkskapitalisme and the state's role in industrial and homeland development.

state-harmful.rationale: Apartheid relied on a powerful state to classify, remove and control people.

strong-leader.rationale: Verwoerd's dominant premiership, which pushed through the republic and homeland policy, was admired by supporters; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The Suppression of Communism, Terrorism and Internal Security acts gave the state wide security powers justified by threats to order.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from nationalist economic upliftment aims.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred: the movement sought to build Afrikaner capital and had no redistributive programme.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred: not a stated position of a state-centred movement.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; an order-preserving, Calvinist movement had no stated view on technology as a cure-all.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Verwoerd's policy sought separation, not expansion.

total-state.rationale: The state controlled much of life through race laws, but not as a total-state doctrine.

traditional-family.rationale: Afrikaner Calvinism held the family and church-centred Christian community as foundational.

unions-good.rationale: The Suppression of Communism Act let the Justice Minister bar people from union office, showing hostility to independent labour organising.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Apartheid-era services were organised by racial group rather than as a universal entitlement; inferred, not a stated position.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Homeland citizenship stripped Africans of South African claims, so benefits followed group status; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed directly: Afrikaner capital pooling coexisted with white landholding.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: collective worker ownership is a socialist idea, and socialism was treated as communism and suppressed.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: a communist form that the state suppressed.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred: white workers were organised within Afrikaner nationalism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Inferred: apartheid ideology saw the state as the instrument of the Afrikaner volk and white nation, not of an economic class, and its anti-communist laws targeted Marxist class analysis.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred: the government pursued energy self-sufficiency under sanctions, but the doctrine itself did not address fossil fuels.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from Afrikaner nationalism's emphasis on one volk, language and culture for the white nation; immigrants were expected to fit in.

elite-replacement.rationale: The regime's feared plot was communist and 'total onslaught', not elite-driven immigration; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: The National Party won power in 1948 under a district system and showed no interest in proportional representation; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Separate development held that each nation should keep its own units and system, so exporting one's government was not the aim; Christian-national calling concerned Afrikaner survival.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Calvinist Christian-national thought upheld traditional gender roles and did not recognise male advantage as a problem; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Adherents held power and defended their own leadership; their grievances were aimed at British, liberal and communist influence; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Racial purity laws were central, but Calvinist Christian-national thought did not back state control of individual reproduction; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The state rejected outside judgment, left the Commonwealth and distrusted the UN, and its security laws protected officials.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The apartheid state regulated where people lived, worked and studied and intervened heavily in the economy and society.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Prohibition of Mixed Marriages Act and the Immorality Act outlawed marriage and sex across racial lines as part of racial separation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The system classified people by race and gave white South Africans rights and power denied to others, rejecting equal standing.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Inferred: the regime was fiercely anti-communist and gave no weight to socialist theory, so it would reject the claim.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Afrikaner nationalism treated the Afrikaners as a people of the land, with a divine calling, rather than as foreign colonists.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred: law was differentiated by racial and ethnic group, with separate legal arrangements for Africans, so a common civil law was not the aim.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred: Christian-national thinking favoured the Reformed churches and mission control; limits on conversion are not documented in the sources.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: no cattle-slaughter ban formed part of the doctrine, and Afrikaner pastoral culture prized beef and meat.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Christian-National Education was the basis of white schooling, and Bantu Education was run along mission and Christian lines.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred: the statement concerns a socialist state, which apartheid adherents opposed; they did favour a strong security state, which cuts the other way.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Verwoerd justified white rule by trusteeship and the nation's calling, and Black Africans were denied a vote in the white state.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred: the Christian-national doctrine presented its racial order as objective truth and divine mandate, not as a product of power.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred from Afrikaner economic nationalism and the aim of national self-sufficiency; trade balance was not a stated doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: Group Areas removals and the assignment of Black Africans to homelands with loss of South African citizenship moved populations out of white areas as a matter of policy.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The state used sweeping security laws and force to uphold the racial order, treating security as justifying coercion.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Inferred from Afrikaner nationalism's framing of the volk's survival as a struggle between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Suppression of Communism Act 1950 outlawed the Communist Party and the government later banned the ANC and PAC.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Inferred: baasskap, white minority domination over the majority, is the opposite of non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred: parliamentary sovereignty and an executive-led security state concentrated power, though the system kept formal institutions.

vanguard-party.rationale: Inferred: the National Party was an ethnic-nationalist party and hostile to revolutionary communism, so it rejects the premise.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred: policy ranked groups by race, not by need, and Bantu Education and homelands gave Black South Africans less.

missingStatements.text: The law should classify people by race and keep the races separate in where they live, study and use public facilities.
missingStatements.rationale: Race classification and legal residential, educational and amenity segregation were the core of the system.

missingStatements.text: Communist parties and organisations should be banned.
missingStatements.rationale: The Suppression of Communism Act outlawed the Communist Party and defined communism broadly.
missingStatements.declined: Anti-communist bans are better captured by existing statements on class struggle and political violence; adding would not separate apartheid from many other ideologies.

notes: Defenders (the baasskap faction, Verwoerd's separate-development faction and the 'purists') differed on how far to separate while still using Black labour. Critics and later scholarship treat its racial premises as a justification for systematic discrimination.
